captions.instagram:
How does the eye see?

Your eye is a 24 mm camera that focuses by changing the shape of a living lens, turns light into signals with 120 million rods and 6 million cones, and even has a blind spot you never notice. Trace real light rays through a 3D eye, try on glasses, and find your own blind spot.

→ Your eye is a 24 mm ball of clear jelly, turned by six muscles.
→ Light passes the cornea, the pupil and the lens, and lands on the retina at the back.
→ The cornea does two-thirds of the focusing. The lens rounds up to focus on near things.
→ After about 45 the lens stiffens, and the picture of a near book stays blurry.
→ A short-sighted eye is too long, so light meets in front of the retina. A concave lens fixes it.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/eyeclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the eye see? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
Your eye is a 24 mm camera that focuses by changing the shape of a living lens, turns light into signals with 120 million rods and 6 million cones, and even has a blind spot you never notice. Trace real light rays through a 3D eye, try on glasses, and find your own blind spot.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox-production-fd52.up.railway.app/e/eyeclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/eyeclear

In this video:
• A camera made of jelly. Light enters through the clear cornea, passes the pupil in the coloured iris, and is focused by the lens onto the retina at the back of a 24 mm ball of clear jelly.
• The cornea does most of the focusing. The eye has about 60 dioptres of focusing power.
• Why we need reading glasses. The lens stiffens with age.
• A millimetre too long. In short sight the eyeball is usually too long, so distant light focuses in front of the retina; each extra millimetre is roughly 3 dioptres.
• Rods, cones and the blind spot. About 120 million rods see in dim light but not in colour; about 6 million cones, packed into the fovea, give colour and detail.
• Three cones make every colour. S, M and L cones peak near 420, 530 and 560 nm, and the brain reads colour from the pattern of their signals.
• Keeping eyes healthy. Cataract, a clouded lens, is the leading cause of blindness worldwide and in India, and surgery replaces it with a clear plastic lens.
